blocks.text: Asthma is chronic airway inflammation with variable, reversible airflow obstruction. Triggers (allergens, cold air, exercise, infections, smoke) cause bronchoconstriction, mucosal swelling and mucus. Symptoms vary over time and are often worse at night or early morning.
Wheeze, chest tightness, breathlessness, cough (often nocturnal), symptoms with exercise or triggers, normal between episodes when well controlled.
Triggers; night waking; reliever (blue inhaler) use frequency; preventer use; previous severe attacks, ICU admission; exercise-related symptoms; personal action plan; inhaler technique.

blocks.label: STOP AND THINK
body: A "silent chest" in an asthma attack is not improvement. It means very little air is moving. This is life-threatening.

steps: **Well controlled?** Exercise training, breathing retraining if dysfunctional breathing, inhaler and action plan education.
**Exercise-induced symptoms?** Warm-up strategy, pre-exercise reliever as prescribed, medical review if frequent.

items: **Breathing retraining** (for example Buteyko-informed or physiotherapy-led programs): nasal breathing, slower and lower breathing, relaxation; improves symptoms and quality of life in some patients [Ref – to verify]. **Exercise**: aerobic training improves fitness and may improve control. Warm up gradually for 10 to 15 minutes, use interval or low-to-moderate continuous efforts, avoid cold dry air or use a mask, cool down slowly. **Education**: inhaler technique with spacer, action plan, trigger avoidance.

blocks.text: Asthma Control Test, PEF diary, exercise tolerance, Nijmegen score.

items: **What does a silent chest mean?** Severe obstruction; life-threatening.
**How can exercise-induced symptoms be reduced?** Warm-up, prescribed pre-exercise reliever, avoid cold dry air.
**Why check inhaler technique?** Poor technique is a common cause of poor control.
**What is dysfunctional breathing?** An abnormal breathing pattern (upper chest, rapid, sighing) causing symptoms, sometimes alongside asthma.
**When is PEF useful?** Tracking variability and recognising deterioration against the personal best.

sections.title: Now You Should Be Able To

items: Recognise acute severe and life-threatening asthma.
Teach breathing retraining and exercise strategies.
Check inhaler technique and support an action plan.
